### Time Grows Short
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/time-grows-short
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:29–31
Points:
- Paul’s pastoral counsel recognized both immediate crisis and the temporary nature of this created order.
- Believers are urged not to conduct their lives as though earthly arrangements are permanent.
- While Christians may gratefully enjoy God’s creation, they must not become inordinately attached to it.
- Present relationships, griefs, and worldly possessions must be held loosely in view of the coming eternal kingdom.

### Because the Time Is Short
Author: Michael A. Youssef, Ph.D.
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/leading-the-way/leading-the-way-devotional-for-august-10-2026.html
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:29
Points:
- Earthly difficulties and the brevity of time urge believers to maintain singleness of heart toward God.
- Surrendering our own agendas enables the Lord to work powerfully for His kingdom and our good.
- Because the world in its present form is fading, Christians should pursue contentment in every circumstance.
- Neither sorrow, nor transient happiness, nor material possessions should be allowed to dominate our devotion.

### Free Yourself from Divided Interests
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/free-yourself-from-divided-interests
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:31
Points:
- Human life is fleeting, and the present form of this world is rapidly passing away.
- Divided interests bring unnecessary anxieties and dilute our capacity for wholehearted kingdom service.
- Undivided devotion requires discerning our current calling while humbly accepting our personal limitations.
- Faithfulness often requires saying a firm "no" to good but nonessential distractions.
- Conducting a regular life audit helps us divest from clutter and live lean for eternal gains.
